Cándido has engaged deeply with Indigenous communities, including strengthening the governance and institutional capacity of 27 Indigenous territories in seven Amazon countries and collaborating with COICA (a regional consortium representing Indigenous communities in the Amazon). He has also contributed to the development of the Amazon Indigenous Women’s Fellowship, an initiative that supports Indigenous women in strengthening their leadership skills and networks across the Amazon.

Before joining Conservation International, Candido worked at CARE, the World Bank, Catholic Relief Services (CRS) and the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) in Bolivia. He earned his bachelor’s degree in communication and development from Catholic Bolivian University.
